item.text:
The affected SDK versions were:

- npm `@mistralai/mistralai`: `2.2.2`, `2.2.3`, `2.2.4`
- npm `@mistralai/mistralai-azure`: `1.7.1`, `1.7.2`, `1.7.3`
- npm `@mistralai/mistralai-gcp`: `1.7.1`, `1.7.2`, `1.7.3`
- PyPI `mistralai`: `2.4.6`

If you installed one:

1. Stop using it immediately and remove/replace it with a non-affected version.
2. Clean any systems where it was installed.
3. Rotate all secrets accessible from those systems.
4. Review cloud audit logs for suspicious activity.
5. Check lockfiles, caches, build artifacts, container images, and private mirrors.
6. Monitor for the indicators listed in Mistral’s remediation guidance.

The PyPI package could execute credential-harvesting code on import under Linux; Mistral says the compromised npm packages were nonfunctional, but still recommends removing them. [Mistral security advisory MAI-2026-002](https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/security-advisories/MAI-2026-002)
